source_text: Σὺ δὲ ἀναστάς, ὦ φίλη κεφαλή, καὶ εὐξάμενος, ἤδη πέμπε ἡμᾶς, σώσας μὲν παρόντας τοῖς ἱεροῖς σου μαθήμασι, σῴζων δὲ ταῖς εὐχαῖς καὶ ἀποδημήσαντας· καὶ δὴ παραδίδου καὶ παρατίθεσο, μᾶλλον δὲ παραδίδου τῷ ἀγαγόντι ἡμᾶς πρὸς σὲ Θεῷ· εὐχαριστῶν μὲν ἐπὶ τοῖς φθάνουσιν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν· παρακαλῶν δὲ χειραγωγεῖν καὶ ἐν τοῖς μέλλουσι, διὰ παντὸς ἐφεστῶτα, ὑπηχοῦντα τῷ νῷ ἡμῶν τὰ αὐτοῦ προστάγματα, ἐμβάλλοντα ἡμῖν τὸν θεῖον φόβον αὐτοῦ παιδαγωγὸν ἄριστον ἐσόμενον. οὐ γὰρ ἐν τῇ μετὰ σοῦ ἐλευθερίᾳ, καὶ ἀπελθόντες ὑπακουσόμεθα αὐτῷ. παρακάλεσον καὶ παραμυθίαν τινὰ ἡμῖν γενέσθαι παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ τῆς ἀπολείψεώς σου· πομπὸν ἀγαθὸν ἐξαποστεῖλαι, συνοδοιπόρον ἄγγελον. αἴτησον δέ, καὶ ἵνα ἐπιστρέψας ἡμᾶς, ἀγάγῃ πρὸς σὲ πάλιν. καὶ τοῦτό γε μάλιστα πάντων, μόνον ἡμᾶς παραμυθήσεται.
thought_title: Farewell prayer: send us off under God's care
orientation: Gregory asks Origen to pray for him and to commit him to the care of God, who led him there.
pass_a_gloss: But you, having risen, O dear head, and having prayed, now send us, having saved us present by your sacred teachings, and saving by prayers also [us] having gone abroad; and now hand over and entrust, or rather hand over to the God who led us to you; giving thanks for the past things for us; and calling on [him] to lead by the hand also in the things to come, through all standing over [us], sounding into our mind his commands, casting into us his divine fear, about to be the best tutor. For not in the freedom with you, also having departed, shall we obey him. Call on [him] also that some comfort come to us from him for the leaving of you; to send out a good escort, a fellow-traveler angel. And ask also that having turned us, he lead us to you again. And this indeed most of all, alone will comfort us.

pass_b_english: But you, my dear friend, rise and pray, and now send us on our way. As you saved us while we were with you by your sacred teachings, save us by your prayers once we have gone away. Hand us over and commit us; or rather, hand us over to the God who led us to you. Give him thanks for what he has already done for us, and ask him to lead us by the hand in what is to come as well: to stand over us always, to whisper his commands to our minds, and to instill in us his divine fear, which will be the best of tutors. For once we have gone away, it will not be in the freedom we had with you that we obey him. Ask him also that some comfort may come to us from him for our parting from you: that he send a good escort, an angel to travel with us. And ask, too, that he turn us back and bring us to you again. This above all, and this alone, will comfort us.
notes: No Scripture is quoted. Left uncited as uncertain: the 'fellow-traveler angel' may echo Raphael in Tobit 5; 'commit us' (παρατίθεσο) may echo Acts 20:32 ('I commend you to God'); 'tutor' (παιδαγωγός) may echo Galatians 3:24. 'ὦ φίλη κεφαλή' (literally 'O dear head', a Homeric form of address) is rendered 'my dear friend'. 'εὐχαριστῶν ... ἐπὶ τοῖς φθάνουσιν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν' may mean thanking God on our behalf or for his past favors to us; 'give him thanks for what he has already done for us' keeps both. Pronouns for God are lower case, matching the rest of this book. Doubtful reading: 'ἐμβάλλοντα' (present) has an unclear ligature; ἐμβαλόντα (aorist) is possible and does not change the sense. 'οὐ γὰρ ἐν τῇ μετὰ σοῦ ἐλευθερίᾳ, καὶ ἀπελθόντες ὑπακουσόμεθα αὐτῷ': the negative governs the phrase 'in the freedom with you', not the obeying itself (facing Latin 'non enim eadem qua apud te libertate, etiam digressi, obediemus illi'); the English word order makes that scope explicit. ἀπόλειψις is rendered 'our parting from you'. ὑπηχοῦντα is rendered 'whisper' (sound in the mind). This is the end of the oration.
